headline: Tabled: Lawrence police Flock camera item and shooting statistics review.
summary: Police presented on the department's 35 Flock license plate cameras, which cost $105,000 a year to lease. They also reviewed shooting statistics from 2024 through October 15, 2026. Both items were tabled.
decisions: Tabled the Lawrence Police Department Flock Safety Cameras item, 3-0, with one member absent.
Tabled the Lawrence Police Department shooting statistics and public safety technology item, 3-0, with one member absent.
discussion: Flock camera privacy and use: Members asked whether the cameras capture faces or support immigration enforcement. Police said the cameras take a still photo of a vehicle's rear, do not use facial recognition, and are not used for immigration enforcement.

Flock audits and discipline: Members asked how misuse is checked and what discipline would follow. Police said one complaint had been received since 2021 and the officer was exonerated, and that discipline would be decided case by case.
Camera removals in other towns: Members asked why Lowell and Methuen removed their Flock cameras. Police said the Lawrence department was not involved in those decisions.

Shooting trends and hotspots: Members asked about the drop in gang-related shootings and the area with the most incidents. Police said a central area of the city has been a hotspot since at least 2018 and that ShotSpotter is used there.

ShotSpotter sensors on private property: Members asked whether sensors are mounted on residents' homes. Police said a few sensors are on private property under agreements with the residents, and that the equipment is leased and renewed each year.

decision_evidence.quote: To table. Okay, can I get a second? ... Thank you, motion carries.
Motion to table. Can I get a second? ... Thank you, motion carries.
